title: Register and read immutable activation definitions
summary: Read or register exact schedules, top-level launch images, literal process context, output paths, immutable identity, and artifact-verification limits.
use_when: A product runner must be represented as one strict immutable schedule and launch context before selection.
The meaning of definition fields, artifact identity, accepted paths, or verification limits is needed.
do_not_use_when: A selected binding should be changed or run; use the binding or activation feature.
The caller needs arbitrary commands, mutable selectors, secrets, workflows, or transitive executable attestation.
outcome: One fully validated immutable definition or its retained exact metadata.
effects: Registration validates direct artifacts and stores private immutable metadata; it can initialize an empty unversioned local schema-two store.
List and show read retained definitions. Registration neither runs a child nor changes a selected binding.
authority: Clockwork owns definition identity and local direct-image admission. The product owns its complete release, domain work, and success.
success: Exact normalized content returns the same digest; changed content receives a distinct immutable identity.
failure_and_recovery: Unsafe paths, hashes, permissions, unknown fields, or policy reject registration. Correct the product candidate without bypassing checks.
privacy: Paths, arguments, schedules, digests, and exact non-secret environment remain private metadata; credentials and product output bodies are prohibited.
does_not_authorize: Operating a binding, running a product, deploying a release, putting credentials in metadata, or treating artifact checks as domain success.

consumers.statement: A current-user operator or product deployer may register or inspect an exact immutable non-agent runner definition.

preconditions.statement: The current-user-owned regular non-symbolic UTF-8 TOML file is at most 1 MiB and not group/world writable; all admitted paths, artifacts, permissions and hashes satisfy the complete feature manual.

inputs.statement: Supported manifest schemas one and two supply stable owner/name key, exact caller-published release ID and canonical release root, direct or interpreted pinned launch images, literal arguments, scrubbed non-secret environment, canonical cwd, private distinct outputs, interval or daily local-calendar trigger, current-user-background authority, skip overlap, optional timeout, and schema-two failure configuration.
PATH lookup, shell strings, mutable selectors, interpolation, inherited environment, implicit shebang choice, literal -c, secrets, and caller runtime argv are unsupported.

outputs.statement: Public commands print plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact ok:true/data JSON envelope and coded ok:false/error JSON on stderr with exit one. Machine callers must pass --json.

Registration returns the SHA-256 digest of canonical JSON for the fully concrete normalized manifest. List returns output-version-two items/has_more with default 20 and positive --limit; show returns full retained metadata.

data_semantics.statement: A definition is an immutable complete launch snapshot; its executable is only the directly verified top-level launch image. Clockwork pins the product-published release identity without recomputing the whole release tree.

identity_and_units.statement: Keys contain two at-most-63-byte lowercase components mapped to org.clockwork.owner.name. Release IDs are canonical UUIDs or retained 64-lowercase-hex IDs. Artifact and definition identities remain 64-lowercase-hex digests. Intervals and optional timeouts use 1 through 31,536,000 whole seconds; local-calendar uses hour 0 through 23 and minute 0 through 59.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Registration validates the complete manifest and direct images before storing a row. Reads select retained definitions at invocation. Activations separately reverify images before execution.
No retention horizon or future artifact validity is promised.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the current-user local CLI and provider-owned clockwork::api types/codecs/client; structural decoding does not perform registration checks.
Direct SQLite integration, same-user authentication by key, root/system execution, or transitive attestation is unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Identical normalized registration is idempotent; changed meaning creates a new definition and requires explicit binding selection. Existing definitions and history are not rewritten.

operational_limits.statement: The manifest is at most 1 MiB and describes one interval or local daily trigger and one launch image profile. Direct programs have recognized Mach-O/fat magic but no complete loader preflight; script and interpreter are separately hashed.
Clockwork does not attest libraries, later configuration, subprocesses, network peers, same-user tampering after verification, or product meaning.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Manifest schemas one and two, SQLite schema two, provider release, product release identity and definition digest are independent. Schema-one definitions retain digest and legacy behavior after storage migration.
No deprecation interval, retention duration or cross-release migration window is promised.

reliances.statement: Artifact publication and concrete runner semantics belong to the registering product; the selected product contract is not enumerated by this generic feature.
